knowledgePattern: Represent roots in a fixed ratio and compare their sum and product

hints.title: Name roots with the required ratio
hints.body: Express the two roots using one unknown scale factor. Then compare their product with the constant term divided by the leading coefficient.
hints.recap: For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, the root product is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and their sum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: The polynomial is not monic; account for its leading coefficient.
hints.pause: Use the product to constrain the scale factor.

recall.reminder: For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>A</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, the root product is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math> and their sum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></math>.

hints.title: Use the sum for the parameter
hints.body: Use the root sum to connect that same scale factor to the coefficient being asked about.
hints.recap: A ratio can be represented by common multiples before using another condition.
hints.pitfall: Do not discard a negative scale factor merely because the ratio is positive.
hints.pause: Combine your two relations to find the requested square.

recall.reminder: A ratio can be represented by common multiples before using another condition.

solution:
1. Write the roots as r and 3r. Their product is 24/2=12, so 3r2=12 and r2=4.

2. Their sum is 4r=−p/2, so p=−8r. Therefore p2=64r2=256. Answer A.

3. Both signs r=2 and r=−2 give distinct real roots and the same requested square.
